name: Hu Shuangmei
current_role: Co-founder and Vice President (per 2019 filing), GoerTek Inc. (SZSE: 002241)
profile: Hu Shuangmei co-founded GoerTek, the Weifang, Shandong acoustics/VR/AR components maker and major Apple/Meta supplier, in 2001 with her husband, chairman Jiang Bin. A Harbin Institute of Technology graduate, she has held management roles at the company and is listed as a vice president; her wealth is shared with Jiang Bin.
interesting_fact: She and Jiang Bin started GoerTek in 2001; the company grew from a microphone maker in Weifang into one of the world's largest makers of acoustic components and VR/AR headsets.
deep_cut_fact: A Harbin Institute of Technology graduate, she joined GoerTek in 2001 as manager of its marketing department and later led its operations leadership group before becoming vice president.
notes: Low public profile; husband Jiang Bin is the public face. Current (post-2025) title not re-verified. Route via GoerTek corporate contact.

name: Sir Anwar Pervez
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Bestway Group (nephew Lord Zameer Choudrey is chairman)
profile: Rawalpindi-born Sir Anwar Pervez (b. 1935) moved to the UK in 1956, drove buses in Bradford, opened a London grocery and built Bestway into a cash-and-carry, pharmacy (Well), cement and banking (UBL) group employing ~47,000. He turned 90 in 2025 and is now Founder & Chairman Emeritus.
interesting_fact: For his 90th birthday in June 2025 King Charles and Queen Camilla hosted him for tea in the Royal Box at Royal Ascot; Bestway also marked its 50th anniversary with an 800-guest event at the Royal Albert Hall.
deep_cut_fact: His first paid job was as a telephone operator for Pakistan's state telecom PTCL, earning 96 rupees a month, before he emigrated and worked double shifts as a Bradford bus conductor for about £16-18 a week.
notes: Aged 91; approach via Bestway Group head office (Park Royal, London). Founded Bestway Foundation in 1987.

name: Lin Su-hon
current_role: Co-founder and President (總裁), Chang Chun Group (Taiwan)
profile: Lin Shu-hong (林書鴻), born c.1927-28, co-founded Taiwan's privately held Chang Chun Group in 1949 with Liao Ming-kun and Cheng Hsin-yi. The never-listed group is a major petrochemical and specialty-chemicals maker whose electronic-grade chemicals supply TSMC, Apple and Tesla. He was still active as group president in his 90s.
interesting_fact: Chang Chun's electronic-grade hydrogen peroxide and wafer developers are supplied to TSMC; at 93 he said he still started his day at 4:30 a.m., using 'one day as three'.
deep_cut_fact: He personally led construction of Chang Chun's Miaoli (Xishan Industrial Zone) plant and spent 10-20 years stationed there in its early days; he was elected one of ITRI's first Laureates in 2012.
notes: Hurun lists him as China but he is Taiwanese. Very private; group is unlisted. Most recent news found is 2021 (age 93), alive status assumed but not freshly confirmed. ITRI laureate claim from search summary, not opened directly. Approach via Chang Chun Group corporate (ccp.com.tw).

name: Brost families
current_role: Former 50% co-owners of WAZ Mediengruppe (now Funke Mediengruppe); stake sold 2012
profile: The Brost family owned half of Essen's WAZ media group, co-founded in 1948 by journalist Erich Brost (d. 1995) with Jakob Funke. After Anneliese Brost's death in 2010 the stake passed to Erich Brost's grandchildren, who sold it to Petra Grotkamp (Funke heirs) in January 2012 for a reported ~EUR 500m.
interesting_fact: Erich Brost worked for the BBC's German service in London during WWII exile and, returning in 1945, helped set up the German News Service that became dpa; his SPD Control Council post was later taken by Willy Brandt.
deep_cut_fact: Anneliese Brost's will created the Brost-Stiftung (founded June 2011, Essen), which funds culture, journalism and social projects in the Ruhr region.
notes: Family entry, not a living individual: Erich Brost died 1995, Anneliese Brost died 2010; heirs are private grandchildren (not profiled). Family exited media in 2012. Brost-Stiftung is a charity, not a family office. Low relevance for podcast.
